London, 21<sup>st</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Europe’s car industry** faces collapse without rapid intervention from EU governments, Carlos Ghosn, Renault’s chief executive, warned today. His comments came as the French government prepared to inject capital into both Renault and Peugeot Citroen on top of the €1bn in loan guarantees given to their finance arms.  Separately, BMW confirmed it was considering tapping Berlin’s €500bn bank liquidity package for its own finance/leasing arm.  Sergio Marchionne, Fiat’s chief executive, indicated there will be only half a dozen global auto-manufacturers left within five years, while the French government is talking of six to eight.  Ghosn’s intervention is the most dramatic plea from Europe’s auto industry for aid to match that given to General Motors and Chrysler, with Ford waiting in the wings.  ACEA wants €40bn in support; the European Investment Bank, the EU’s in-house lender, has made €10bn available over the next two years in soft loans.  French car sales held up last year but began to fall off a cliff towards the end of the year. _The EU industry fears overall sales could collapse by 20% this year. Source:  Guardian_ 

**Fiat, Chrysler, and Cerberus** announced that they have signed a non-binding agreement to establish a global strategic alliance. The alliance would provide Chrysler with access to competitive, fuel-efficient vehicle platforms, powertrain, and components to be produced at Chrysler manufacturing sites. Fiat would provide distribution capabilities in key growth markets, cost saving opportunities, and management services supporting Chrysler’s submission of a viability plan to the US Treasury, as required under the financial bailout plan for US auto manufacturers.  Fiat would receive an initial 35% equity interest in Chrysler. The alliance does not contemplate that Fiat would make a cash investment in Chrysler, or commit to funding Chrysler in the future. _Source:  Engineering Weekly_ 

**Toyota** is poised to end GM’s 77-year reign as the world’s largest automaker after avoiding the worst of the meltdown in global auto demand. GM’s 2008 sales probably fell by over 10 % to about 8.34 million vehicles. Toyota posted a 4 % drop to 8.92 million. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**North American Palladium** has increased the indicated resource estimate at the Offset zone of its Lac des Iles PGM mine, in Thunder Bay, Ontario, by 280%.  The indicated resource for the Offset high-grade zone is now 12,3 million tons. A preliminary assessment in May last year said that the Offset zone could be mined for up to ten years, and may yield annual production of 250koz of palladium, 16koz of platinum, 17k oz of gold, 2-million pounds of nickel and 4-million pounds of copper.  A detailed prefeasibility study is under way, and should be completed by mid-year.  Lac Des Iles was shut in October last year, as it was losing money because of low PGM prices.  However, in the meantime, the

company plans an “aggressive” drilling programme.  North American Palladium had $106-million in working capital at the end of September08, and has “minimal” debt.  The firm will take advantage of its strong balance sheet “as it also evaluates acquisition and joint venture opportunities in 2009”. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Platinum prices** will see little benefit this year from a widely anticipated fall in supply, as cost and operational concerns discourage South African producers from closing down their mines. While analysts agree that production is unsustainable at present price levels of under $1,000 an ounce, the costs of scaling back output are keeping mines running for now, even at a loss.  Miners are weighing up the cost of closing down plants and of restarting them when demand for platinum improves against the prospects for a long-term downturn in prices, and choosing to maintain their current operations, analysts said.  This makes it unlikely that production will fall significantly -- if at all -- this year. _Source:  Guardian_
